cards.explanation: The answer is larger and stronger than Israel. Moses doesn't sugarcoat it. He calls them “…seven nations larger and stronger than you…” So Israel is the underdog in this picture, and I think Moses is building toward something with that. Keep this one in your pocket, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, “Make no treaty with them and show them no mercy.” He doesn't leave a door cracked open for a deal. It's one of the plainest lines in the whole passage (Deuteronomy 7:2).

The answer is intermarry. Moses says, “Do not intermarry with them.” He spells it out, too: Israel isn't to give their daughters to the nations' sons or take the nations' daughters for their own sons. It's a clear line, friends, and no one has to guess at it.

The answer is that they would turn Israel's sons away to serve other gods. Moses passes along God's words, and God says, “…they will turn your sons away from following Me to serve other gods.” The "Me" is the LORD Himself. So the question is whose voice Israel's sons would end up following. Then the words say, “Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will swiftly destroy you.” (Deuteronomy 7:4)

The answer is to burn them in the fire. Moses says, “…burn their idols in the fire.” The altars, pillars and poles each get their own action, and the idols get the fire. Verse 5 reads like a full work order, friends.

The answer is His prized possession. Moses says the LORD has chosen Israel “…to be a people for His prized possession out of all peoples on the face of the earth.” Out of every people on earth, He picked them. That's the heart of verse 6.

The answer is False. Moses says the LORD did not choose Israel because they were more numerous, “…for you were the fewest of all peoples.” Numbers didn't win Israel the spot. Hold onto that, friends, because Moses gives the real reason next.

The answer is loved. Moses says, “…the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers…” Israel was the fewest of all peoples, so it wasn't their numbers (Deuteronomy 7:7). I know a little about being picked when nobody was counting. A quarter, a closing bakery bin, and Mother Miller smiling at me.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD is “…the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations…” and he says it's for those who love Him and keep His commandments. A thousand generations is a long, long time, friends. That's a lot of keeping.

The answer is to keep the commandments Moses is giving them. That's the conclusion he draws from everything he's said about the LORD. He says, “So keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances that I am giving you to follow this day.” It all leads to that one word: keep. Verse 11 is the landing spot, friends.

The answer is their children and their land and their flocks. Moses says the LORD will bless “…your grain, new wine, and oil, the young of your herds and the lambs of your flocks…” and he's talking about children too. So the family, the harvest and the animals all get covered in Deuteronomy 7:13. That's a full pantry, friends.
The answer is True. Moses says, “And the LORD will remove from you all sickness.” He adds that Israel won't be given the terrible diseases they knew in Egypt. All means all in that sentence, friends.

The answer is a snare to Israel. Moses says, “Do not worship their gods, for that will be a snare to you.” A snare is a trap, and it catches the one who walks into it. He says the trap would be for Israel.

The answer is remember. Moses says, “Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt…” He tells them not to be afraid and to look back instead. I've been known to search for my hat while wearing it, so I respect anyone who sets up a reminder.

The answer is the hornet. Moses says, “Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet against them until even the survivors hiding from you have perished.” Even the ones hiding don't get away, friends. The text gives only that one word for it.

The answer is False. Moses says, “The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you little by little.” He also says Israel will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once. A little at a time is how verse 22 puts it.

The answer is that the wild animals would multiply around Israel. Moses says Israel will not be enabled to eliminate them all at once, “…or the wild animals would multiply around you.” So the pace is little by little. The text gives that one reason, friends.
The answer is False. Moses says, “No one will be able to stand against you…” He doesn't leave a few nations standing. It comes right after he says the LORD will hand their kings over to Israel.

The answer is that it is detestable to the LORD. Moses says not to covet the silver and gold on the images “…or you will be ensnared by it; for it is detestable to the LORD your God.” So Israel is to burn the images and leave the metal alone. That's the stated reason in verse 25, friends.

The answer is destruction. Moses says, “And you must not bring any detestable thing into your house, or you, like it, will be set apart for destruction.” It's a heavy line, friends, and he says it plainly. He means it as a warning to keep that thing out of the house.
